articles.title: Hundreds of protests expected across France, with shops, businesses and tourist sites closed – Europe live
articles.description: France will deploy 70,000 officers around the country. Protests are also expected in Italy, Spain, Austria, Portugal, Albania and Ireland Following last weekend’s unrest, authorities across France moved to try to restrict demonstrations, limiting gathering numbers and march routes and issuing blanket bans in some cities. That led to groups seeking permission for “authorised” protests with mixed results. For example, in Paris, the leading trade union was granted permission for their march while the Yellow Vest demonstrators were denied. Paris, Lille, Strasbourg, Mulhouse, Grenoble, Toulouse, Amiens

articles.title: British woman dies trying to save sons on Bahamas snorkelling trip
articles.description: The 36-year-old died after two boys reportedly swept away by strong current near Bimini, police say A British woman has died in the Bahamas while trying to rescue her two sons after a current swept them away as they were snorkelling. The Royal Bahamas police force said it had launched an investigation after the death of a 36-year-old woman on Tuesday.

articles.title: Kim Jong-un crosses over newly opened bridge into China
articles.description: Visit by train over New Yalu River Bridge marks North Korean leader’s first known trip abroad in more than a year Kim Jong-un has travelled to China over a newly opened bridge marking the North Korean leader’s first known trip abroad in more than a year, South Korean officials have said. A government source told the Yonhap news agency on Saturday that Kim had arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong, in Liaoning province, after taking a train from Pyongyang to Sinuiju and crossing the New Yalu River Bridge.

articles.title: Tinned food, loo roll and power banks: the Brits following advice to stockpile
articles.description: Government campaign recommends three days’ worth of stores for emergencies, but some are ahead of the game Dried foods, bottled water, medicine stocks and backup power banks: it could be the props cupboard on a disaster movie, but instead it is precisely what some UK residents are stockpiling amid official warnings about Russian “state-sponsored terrorism” and the impact of the climate crisis. The government launched a campaign on Thursday advising people to set aside three days’ worth of stores to deal with a whole range of eventualities, and some are already well under way.

articles.title: Dónal Lunny, ‘colossus of Irish music’, dies aged 79
articles.description: Founding member of Planxty, Lunny went on to play for bands such as Moving Hearts, the Bothy Band and Coolfin The Irish traditional musician Dónal Lunny has died at the age of 79 from cancer. Lunny rose to prominence in the trio Rakes of Kildare alongside his brother Frank and Christy Moore. He went on to play in bands such as Planxty , Moving Hearts , the Bothy Band and Coolfin among others and toured the world.

articles.title: Blue Planet III features cloudier footage to prove authenticity amid AI boom
articles.description: BBC series deliberately uses ‘more organic’ shots to assure viewers animals are not AI-generated, producers say The David Attenborough -narrated series Blue Planet III deliberately includes cloudier, less polished footage to counter AI fakery and assure viewers it is “authentic”, its producers have said. Nearly a decade after Blue Planet II shone a light on plastic pollution, and 25 years since the first Blue Planet aired, the hit BBC series is returning with more animal behaviour and cutting-edge technology, including the world’s first underwater CCTV camera – dubbed “stonefish” cam.

articles.title: ‘You need persistence’: the Norfolk couple who took on environmental regulators three times – and won
articles.description: Tim and Geli Harris have spent more than a decade fighting to protect Catfield Fen, a rare wetland in the Norfolk Broads Polluters and regulators who fail to stop pollution must quake in their boots when they receive a letter from the lawyers for Tim and Geli Harris. The couple, who farm 460 acres in the Norfolk Broads, have now scored a hat-trick of landmark legal victories to save an internationally important wetland after they won again in the high court this month. Lady Justice Lieven found that Natural England failed in its statutory duty to protect Catfield Fen from pollution after nitrates and phosphates washed from arable fields into one of the finest examples of calcareous fen in western Europe, home to 2,500 species including rarities such as the fen orchid, crested buckler fern, breeding bittern and swallowtail butterflies.

articles.title: Opposition deepfake video of Spanish PM’s wife sparks outrage before election
articles.description: Video shows AI likenesses of people linked to Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist party appearing to admit to wrongdoing A political ad from Spain’s main opposition party that used a deepfake video of the prime minister’s wife has sparked outrage and set off a wider debate on AI, as the deeply polarised country gears up for general elections next month. Launched this week across the social media channels of the conservative People’s party (PP), the video used artificial intelligence to manipulate the likenesses of various people linked to Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist party and appeared to show them admitting to acts such as soliciting prostitutes and taking kickbacks.

articles.title: “Culture is stagnant, so politics is stuck” – playwright James Graham | Radical Thinking – podcast
articles.description: Are we doomscrolling our way into a democratic crisis? That’s what the playwright James Graham fears may be happening, as he suggests that our algorithms have led us into ‘a massive crisis of the new’ and are preventing us from imagining a different future Watch the full episode with James Graham here . INK will be released in UK cinemas on 8 January 2027 Aditya suggested reading (and watching) list for James Graham: Dear England : about England’s football team Sherwood : mentioned in the conversation, set in the village where James Graham grew up in the shadow of the miners’ strike Quiz : set on the British quiz show, Who wants to be a millionaire, where a contestant wins a million quid

articles.title: What next for France as riots rattle markets? Three questions facing investors ahead of more protests
articles.description: French unrest pushed bond yields to a 24-year high as investors weigh budget, growth and sectors risks ahead of more protests.

articles.title: Blaze engulfs Hitler’s ‘Eagle’s Nest’ mountain retreat in Bavaria
articles.description: About 200 firefighters deployed to tackle the blaze at former Nazi retreat in a remote part of southern Germany German police said Saturday they had detained a suspect after a fire at Adolf Hitler’s former mountain retreat, known as the Eagle’s Nest, in the state of Bavaria. About 200 firefighters were deployed to tackle the blaze at the Nazi dictator’s remote and difficult-to-access Kehlsteinhaus residence, on the peak of Obersalzberg in southern Germany.

articles.title: More than third of post offices in TG Jones stores to shut by early 2027
articles.description: Closures within chain formerly under the WH Smith brand raise fears of high streets becoming ‘postal deserts’ Towns and even city centres face being left as “postal deserts” after it emerged that more than a third of post offices within the troubled TG Jones chain are closing. So far this year 36 branches within the high street chain formerly known as WH Smith have closed and a further 34 are set to close by early 2027, according to Post Office records analysed by the Guardian.

articles.title: ‘It’s part of our history’: can the menú del día survive Spain’s changing eating habits?
articles.description: Established under the Franco dictatorship, the lunchtime ritual is in decline but all is not lost A little before lunchtime each working day across Spain, evidence of one of the lingering, if less notorious, legacies of the Franco dictatorship is carefully traced in chalk, marker pen and printer ink. Beckoning to hungry workers from blackboards, whiteboards and pieces of paper hastily taped to windows, the competitively priced menú del día , or daily set-price lunch, has been part of everyday Spanish life for more than half a century. But while 4m menús are still served each weekday, Spain is slowly losing its appetite for the familiar ritual.

articles.title: As a divided Israel prepares to go to the polls, can Netanyahu pull off his greatest political trick yet?
articles.description: The prime minister has defined and dominated his country’s politics for three decades and is putting his rivals on the defensive before Tuesday’s general election They chant his name, they cheer and clap – and yet he is not the most dominant person in the room. Looming over the crowd that has gathered to hear Gadi Eisenkot, the former general who is the lead opposition challenger in Tuesday’s Israeli election, is a man who is not there. It is the man Eisenkot seeks to replace as prime minister, the man who first served in that role three decades ago and who has held it, on and off, for 19 of the past 30 years. It is Benjamin Netanyahu. Naturally, the warm-up speakers at this evening rally in the modest city of Modi’in, halfway between Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, stress the virtues of Eisenkot, a son of working-class Moroccan Jews who rose through the ranks to become chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces and entered politics only four years ago. But every sentence might as well end with two words that go unspoken: unlike Bibi .

articles.title: Democrat James Talarico targets Elon Musk at rally: ‘Texas is not for sale’
articles.description: The Senate candidate denounced opponent Ken Paxton, calling out corruption allegations and support from Musk James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for the US Senate in Texas, has taken aim at Elon Musk, warning that the tech mogul is trying to buy political influence and declaring: “Texas is not for sale.” Talarico held a campaign rally on Friday at the University of Texas at Austin, packing an auditorium at his alma mater with hundreds of students and other supporters, who cheered, whooped and waved campaign signs.

articles.title: Typhoon Champi kills one and injures more than 500 in Taiwan as it heads to China
articles.description: Super typhoon weakening but large parts of Taiwan, including Taipei, still mostly closed and flights cancelled Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday killing one person, injuring more than 500, and uprooting trees and severing power as it weakened and ⁠headed north toward ⁠the ​Chinese coast. Earlier classified as a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the ⁠Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of about 126km per hour (78 miles per hour) near its ⁠centre, according to Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA).

articles.title: California officials ordered by DoJ to set aside ‘likely’ noncitizen ballots
articles.description: Letters from federal prosecutors represent latest escalation as Trump continues to make claims of voter fraud Federal prosecutors sent letters to county registrars across California on Friday demanding that local officials set aside and verify ballots that the Department of Justice said may belong to noncitizens, according to the Los Angeles county registrar and a letter obtained by the Associated Press. The letters are the latest escalation in a legal battle between California and Donald Trump’s Department of Justice, which has recently focused on the state in its efforts to root out noncitizen voting ahead of the midterm elections.

articles.title: Seven killed and 40 injured after gunmen open fire at church funeral in Jordan
articles.description: Footage broadcast on state television showed two gunmen who appear to be holding pistols approaching the church and firing shots Eight people were killed on Friday when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan, in a rare attack ⁠on Jordan’s Christian minority that ​authorities described as a terrorist act by extremists. Maj gen Abdallah al-Maaytah, the head of the country’s ⁠Public Security Directorate, said most of those injured in the shooting at St George’s Greek Orthodox church in Hamoud, in Karak governorate, were still receiving treatment, and that the ⁠hunt for the attackers was continuing. Jordan’s health minister said 40 people were injured.

articles.title: Pentagon designates China-backed campus cultural centers a threat to US national security
articles.description: Defense secretary Pete Hegseth alleges Confucius Institutes operating in disguise on US university campuses The ⁠US defense department has designated Chinese-funded cultural centers on university campuses ⁠known as Confucius ⁠Institutes ​as a threat to US national security, defense secretary Pete ⁠Hegseth said on Friday. Washington has long accused Confucius Institutes of being Chinese propaganda ⁠tools and has taken steps to ​crack down on them.

articles.title: Embattled Greens senator Jordon Steele-John confirms leave from parliament after allegations against him made public
articles.description: WA politician says he considered attending Senate estimates virtually but was told it would be ‘unacceptable’ Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast Jordon Steele-John has confirmed he will not attend parliament next week as the embattled Greens senator apologises for publicly releasing the letter outlining the claims against him. On Saturday afternoon, Steele-John removed a social media post containing a three-page letter marked as “confidential” sent to the Greens leader, David Shoebridge, earlier this month. The letter urged an investigation into allegations he had acted inappropriately towards women between 2017 and 2025.

articles.description: US secretary of state makes comments after Trump tells US rally warships could intervene on return from Iran Marco Rubio urged Cubans seeking political change in their country to act, saying “now is the time” moments after Donald Trump told a Friday rally for candidates in south Florida that US warships could intervene in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war. The US secretary of state, in his social media post addressed “to those who seek to create positive change”, urged Cubans to capitalize on Trump’s plans. “The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete [sic] partnership with the CIA,” Rubio said.

articles.title: Father who killed Oregon school shooter speaks out for first time: ‘I have to go in’
articles.description: Kaylub Giamanco recounts the day he confronted the Silver Rail elementary school shooter, who killed three boys and one teacher The Oregon father hailed as a hero for stopping a school shooting last week spoke for the first time about the incident, describing his experience and how he told a 911 operator: “I have to go in. People are going to die.” Kaylub Giamanco, a 36-year-old carpenter, has received national attention and praise for stopping the bloodshed at Silver Rail elementary in Bend, Oregon, where his children attend school.

articles.title: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus
articles.description: Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country. The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.

articles.title: Magnitude-7 earthquake hits Tibet, killing at least 16 and destroying hundreds of homes
articles.description: Search and rescue efforts under way after quake strikes region’s north, with at least seven aftershocks recorded A magnitude-7 earthquake has hit Tibet, killing at least 16 people, injuring 54 and destroying hundreds of homes in the northern regional city of Nagqu, official media have said. Search and rescue efforts continued after at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds collapsed, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials. It was the biggest quake in the region in the past five years, according to China’s national broadcaster CCTV.

articles.title: India slashes cost of cancer drugs after court rules mark-ups are ‘extortion’
articles.description: Case filed in 2022 by patient unable to afford medicine leads to cap on drug prices for millions who face ruin if diagnosed The Indian government has moved to reduce the price of cancer drugs after a retired bank clerk took her case to the supreme court. From next month, 137 cancer drugs in India will be cheaper as the government tries to tackle the tragedy of poorer patients either forgoing treatment, selling land or falling into debt to meet the high cost of some medicines, which are making large profits for hospitals and pharmacists.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix
articles.description: 41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’ Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s . The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record. Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.

articles.description: 星巴克表示，隨著與本土競爭對手展開競爭，公司正致力改善顧客的店內體驗。

articles.title: 暗影人物：與烏克蘭合作的俄羅斯人
articles.description: 從線人和秘密網絡，到破壞行動及暗殺的指控，俄羅斯與烏克蘭之間的戰爭，正越來越多地在遠離戰場的地方展開。 這場暗影戰爭的許多細節難以核實。不過，《BBC之眼》罕有地接觸到一些俄羅斯人。他們聲稱，自己正通過在俄羅斯境內執行行動，以協助烏克蘭。BBC已確認他們為烏克蘭情報機構工作，但未能獨立核實他們所稱參與的行動。

articles.title: 特朗普收緊綠卡政策，印度科技從業者的「美國夢」面臨考驗
articles.description: 由於移民限制和科技公司削減外籍員工，獲得美國永久居留權對許多印度人來說正變得越來越遙不可及。

articles.title: 《決勝時刻》新遊戲設想朝鮮入侵韓國，真的會發生嗎？
articles.description: 在新的《決勝時刻》遊戲中，北韓入侵了南韓。這種情景有多現實？如果真的發生，又會帶來哪些後果？

articles.title: Google軍事人工智能合約引發辭職潮
articles.description: BBC採訪了多名前任和現任Google DeepMind員工，了解他們對人工智能在戰場上應用的憂慮。

articles.title: North Korea prepares to restart propaganda loudspeakers as ties sour with South
articles.description: Kim Yo-jong, sister of Kim Jong-un, issues warning after inspecting border fortifications against backdrop of rising tensions Propaganda loudspeakers aimed at South Korea will be ready to restart within days along the entire border, Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, has said amid a worsening of ties between the two countries. The statement, carried by the state news agency KCNA on Thursday, came a day after she said the loudspeakers would be in operation along the whole border from some time in October.

articles.title: Sovereign wealth funds' China and Hong Kong investments surge 190% after a bruising slump
articles.description: Sovereign wealth funds are pouring billions of dollars back into China after a sharp investment slump.

articles.title: 吃什麼能保持年輕肌膚？
articles.description: 植物、脂肪和發酵食品可以減少皺紋，促進膠原蛋白生長，並改善皮膚質地。

articles.title: 為甚麼馬斯克要策劃 SpaceX 與特斯拉的超大型合併？
articles.description: 馬斯克稱，透過合併這兩家公司，「有很多好處可獲得」，而這將會是歷來規模最大的合併案。

articles.title: 特朗普治下，美國經濟的真實表現如何？
articles.description: 中期選舉前夕，特朗普一直吹噓美國經濟的表現。 BBC事實查核（BBC Verify）調查美國的通貨膨脹、就業和經濟成長。

articles.title: Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted
articles.description: Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’ The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday. It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, wrote on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.”

articles.title: Indian court orders release of two leaders of Cockroach movement
articles.description: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in jail after defying restrictions on protests in Delhi amid government crackdown An Indian court has ordered the release of two leaders of India’s Cockroach movement who were jailed last week amid a mounting state crackdown on youth-led protests. The two leaders of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) movement, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, had spent a week in Delhi’s Tihar jail after being arrested by Delhi police last week.

articles.title: Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say
articles.description: Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two Florida immigration jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions. Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facilities in south Florida.

articles.title: 華東颱風強、印尼野火烈——厄爾尼諾現象影響世界的五個方面
articles.description: 有記錄以來最強的厄爾尼諾現象持續增強之際，全球各地已經感受到哪些天氣模式方面的影響？BBC首席氣象預報員莎拉·基斯—盧卡斯（Sarah Keith-Lucas）檢視相關證據。

articles.title: 翻看英國統計 為何從未吸煙的人也開始對電子煙上癮？
articles.description: 根據英國國家統計局（ONS）數據，目前有超過100萬名電子煙使用者過去從未吸煙。

articles.title: 在實體商店購物很令我心煩——為什麼我只在網上購物
articles.description: 英國服飾零售巨頭Primark首次將推出宅配服務，以應對Shein等超快時尚競爭。網上零售佔比持續上升，專家稱退貨政策成關鍵。

articles.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa
articles.description: Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said. The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.

articles.title: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject plan to leave Canada in referendum
articles.description: Result is a victory for prime minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity Voters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin the process of independence, delivering a decisive victory for supporters of Canadian unity and deepening divisions within the separatist movement. With nearly 1.9m votes counted, roughly 76% people supported remaining in Canada, while 24% backed beginning a process toward separation, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta.

articles.title: 朝鮮發佈金正恩照片：為何他的死亡傳言總是捲土重來？
articles.description: 在未經證實的傳言傳開後，朝鮮官媒發布了這位獨裁者與其女兒的照片。

articles.title: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani launches India’s biggest-ever IPO
articles.description: Low-cost broadband provider Jio Platforms aims for £81bn valuation when it floats on the stock market on Wednesday India’s second-richest man, Mukesh Ambani, is launching what could be the country’s biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), despite a stock market downturn. Mumbai-based Jio Platforms, a telecoms company backed by Meta Platforms and Google, is hoping to raise up to 302bn rupees (£2.4bn) and is targeting a 10.3tn rupees valuation when it floats on the stock market from Wednesday.

articles.title: 普京提議中美俄「三方會談」：特朗普響應，北京未表態，基輔反對
articles.description: 在普京建議三方於APEC期間進行會談後，特朗普表示願意參與，強調會談重點將是無核化問題。目前中方尚未就三方會談表態。

articles.title: DeepSeek被美國政府系統禁用：中美AI競爭繼續升溫
articles.description: DeepSeek的免費聊天機器人應用程式在Apple App Store下載排行榜上名列前茅，其AI模型也被美國科技企業採用。Snowflake、Vercel及OpenRouter等公司都已將DeepSeek整合至其提供給客戶的服務中。

articles.title: She was harassed for crude remarks about Modi at a Cockroach protest. Now she can’t leave home
articles.description: ​After a protest clip went viral, a teenager’s life was torn apart by threats that sent her and her family into hiding. Plus, a book on citizen journalism • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Before 24 July, a person I will call R was preoccupied with the ordinary routines of teenage life: experimenting with makeup, grumbling over mathematics homework and hanging out with friends at a tea stall. That month, as the fever of student protests spread across the country, the 15-year-old watched on her phone as young people poured into Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in Delhi, demanding education reform. She went too. But an 11-second video clip from the protest site, in which she made crude and profane remarks about the prime minister, Narendra Modi, upended her life.

articles.title: 香港演員鍾雪瑩、袁澧林發聲之後，她們親述被性別冒犯的經歷
articles.description: BBC中文訪問了四位來自不同行業的女性，了解言語冒犯是如何在工作環境中出現；當性別冒犯被包裝成「玩笑」，她們是如何應對。

articles.title: 俄羅斯境內反普京破壞行動的隱秘世界
articles.description: 兩名男子講述了他們聲稱在戰爭期間為烏克蘭情報部門提供支援所從事的工作。

articles.title: 《孤獨的美食家》：一個人吃飯，為什麼能紅遍全亞洲？
articles.description: 開播至今14年，《孤獨的美食家》從日本深夜劇成長為風靡亞洲的電視作品。觀眾跟隨主角井之頭五郎穿梭街巷尋找美食和故事。主演松重豐希望讓更多海外觀眾透過美食認識日本文化。

articles.title: 中國三季度增長4.5% 但出口暴增，樓市新開工面積暴跌
articles.description: 分析人士向BBC指出，中國依賴單一外需引擎的風險正在累積，北京的刺激空間有限，未必願意、也未必有能力在這個時點大舉加碼。

articles.title: 尊界V800「煞車門」：從產品安全之爭到「恨國」論戰
articles.description: 華為尊界V800煞車踏板斷裂爭議迅速升溫，從產品安全問題延伸至「速成車」質疑、中美汽車技術比較，以及民族品牌形象之爭。隨著官媒下場評議，事件進一步演變為一場輿論與產業敘事的角力。

articles.title: 遊艇上的水上滑梯、泳池：衛星影像揭示的金正恩「夏宮」生活
articles.description: BBC追蹤了一艘長達80米、配有水上滑梯的船隻，旨在進一步了解金正恩如何度過假期——這對大多數朝鮮人而言，是遙不可及的體驗。

articles.title: 「我擔心得不敢去中國了」：韓國脫北者接連收到警方赴華警告
articles.description: 為何已在韓國定居的脫北者，如今對前往中國感到憂慮？BBC深入了解韓國警方發出旅遊警告的背景，以及脫北者實際遭中國當局拒絕入境的個案。

articles.title: 石油出口放緩之際 霍爾木茲海峽輪船遇襲案件創新高
articles.description: BBC事實查核（BBC Verify）對英國海事機構數據的分析顯示，過去一星期內有12艘船隻遭到襲擊。

articles.title: 「我今年12歲，該嘗試蛋白粉嗎？」
articles.description: BBC詢問專家，兒童和青少年服用蛋白質補充劑是否安全。

articles.title: 美沙冬是毒還是藥？從香港經驗看台灣選戰戒毒爭議
articles.description: 台北市長選舉引發對「美沙冬」（香港稱「美沙酮」）與毒品減害政策的論戰，然而在海峽對岸的香港，這項計劃已運作超過半世紀。為什麼醫學界將其視為有效降低犯罪與血液傳染病的「減害」關鍵？

articles.title: 新鴨綠江大橋閒置12年終開通：中朝關係回暖？
articles.description: 連接中國與朝鮮的鴨綠江大橋，在閒置12年之後終於正式開通。近年朝鮮與俄羅斯關係愈走愈近，專家分析中方需要透過開通大橋鞏固對朝關係，也被視為關係回暖的象徵。

articles.title: 人類身高的起伏變化：哪些歷史事件影響最大？
articles.description: 如今我們的身高比100年前高了大約10厘米，但這並非一帆風順。

articles.title: 台灣選舉解讀：「北藍南綠」的政治版圖是否「鐵板一塊」？
articles.description: 「北藍南綠」是描述台灣政治版圖的常見概念，但近年選舉結果顯示，這樣的區域分野並非一成不變，中間選民的流向在這次地方選舉可能左右大局。

articles.title: 台灣AV盛極而衰：中國市場如何催生這場成人片熱潮？
articles.description: 台灣曾被視為亞洲唯一能合法拍攝無碼成人影片的地區，並在2020年前後快速擴張。隨著片商「麻豆傳媒」停運，外界開始質疑這波繁榮是否與中國市場及博弈資金有關。

articles.title: 「特習會」後兩架美國 F-16V 抵台 「雖遲但到」的時機與信號
articles.description: 本周五，台灣在2019年向美國訂購的2架F-16V戰機先行抵達台灣台東空軍志航基地，同批次共有66架同型號戰機，是1990 年代以來台灣首次戰機採購。

articles.title: 為何特朗普在國宴上送習近平一座華麗的白頭海鵰雕像？
articles.description: 從紅杉木長椅到DVD，饋贈禮物一直是外交藝術的重要一環。

articles.title: 從年輕縣官到國家主席：習近平41年來的訪美影像
articles.description: 習近平即將到訪美國會晤特朗普（川普），這將是他歷來第11次以中國官方身份訪美。從31歲縣委書記到中國國家主席，BBC中文透過歷年照片，回顧他的訪美行程如何隨身份和中美關係變化。

articles.title: 颱風薔琵：台灣釀1死171傷，大部分縣市停班停課
articles.description: 颱風薔琵風暴圈籠罩全台灣，至今造成1死171傷。氣象部門預測，週五（23日）下午至週六（24日）白天風雨最大。中國沿海地區也嚴陣以待。
